Method of lines: finite-volume Laplacian with zero-flux boundaries, explicit Euler steps of 1/steps_per_hour hours in pytensor.scan. The PDE starts from the counts at the first fitted time (conditioned on, not in the likelihood, kept in the bundle). Counts are Poisson with mean K u. Priors: D ~ LogNormal(log 1000, 1) um^2/h, lam ~ LogNormal(log 0.05, 1) 1/h, K ~ Normal(122, 15), beta ~ LogNormal(log 0.1, 1) 1/h. The fit refuses settings where D dt / dx^2 > 1/2 at the 99% prior quantile of D (CFL bound). wave_speed = 2 sqrt(D lam). Without the delay, D is biased low by a factor of about four on the PC-3 data, and LOO prefers the delay model.

assumptions: The mass of the lens is an isothermal ellipsoid, with an optional external shear
The light of the lens galaxy and of the source are smooth elliptical profiles
The noise is Gaussian. Neighbouring pixels can have a correlated noise

about.expert_notes: Pixel forward model in PyTensor: a singular isothermal ellipsoid (Kormann et al. 1994) plus external shear, ray tracing on a sub-pixel grid, Sersic lens light and source, and PSF convolution as a separable SVD expansion (matrix products only). A separable lag-one correlation of the noise (drizzled images) is whitened exactly. The linear light amplitudes are integrated out in closed form and drawn after the fit from their conditional Gaussian. A staged optimisation finds the mode (lens light with sigma clipping, the Einstein radius from the ring profile, then starts around the lens axis). NUTS samples a parameterisation whitened by the Laplace approximation at that mode. Critical curves and caustics are analytic for each direction. The mass-sheet degeneracy is not broken: only the mass inside the Einstein radius is robust. No pointwise LOO.

assumptions: Each actual value is compared with the draws for the same cell
A well-calibrated model puts about 90% of the values inside its 90% range
avoid_when: You want to see the fit over time (use Fit and forecast)

about.example: The coverage line is below the diagonal and only 70% of the values are in the 90% range. The PIT histogram is high at both ends (a U shape). The ranges of the model are too narrow, so the model is too sure.
about.expert_notes: PIT = P(ŷ < y) + ½ P(ŷ = y) per observed cell over the matched draws. The PIT histogram uses `bins` (default 20) and a ±1.96 SD binomial band. Coverage is the share of observations inside central equal-tailed intervals at `levels` (0.1 to 0.95). Caption rules: mean PIT < 0.4 (over-predicts) or > 0.6 (under-predicts); > 20% of PIT values in the outer 10% (too narrow); < 2% with n ≥ 50 (too wide). PIT values are not independent across time, so treat the band as a guide.

A coverage line against the ideal diagonal
A caption with the coverage of the 90% range and warnings
